thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=realtime-routing-canary (PD: PD-8231), severity=critical. Metric: canary eu-west 5xx-rate 27% over 3m, traffic_split=2%. roll_tag=canary:v2.7.0. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-8231
emma: acked (on-call). I'm on it. /me pulling logs and checking canary rollout status :eyes:
pd-bot: Acknowledgement recorded by emma at 1798887782
sam: quick look: 502s originate from tokenizer-service upstream (trace ids sample: 7c3a, 9f1b). Nothing in infra cpu/mem. I see sudden spike right after canary ramp to 2% at 17:24 UTC.
mike: noted. can anyone confirm if the canary gating test ran? I see a missed readiness check in the deploy pipeline output.
lina: customer-impact check: support alerts show 12 complaints in EU-WEST for slow/failed embeddings in last 10m. tagging priority P1. cc @support-engine
support-engine: we have a handful of production customers affected (ids: C-9812, C-4419). They're reporting retries/timeouts. Advising mitigation asap.
emma: plan: 1) suppress duplicate pages (PD is firing multiple escalations due to both canary and routing alerts), 2) roll back canary or pause traffic, 3) divert traffic away from eu-west canary until stable. I'll own suppression + coordination.
sam: logs show tokenizer v3.2.1 returning 502 when batch size>1. Possible regression with batching change in v2.7.0 pipeline. Repro locally with small script.```# repro (local shim)
curl -s -X POST https://eu-west-realtime/realtime/v1/embeddings -d '{"batch":["a","b"]}' | jq .errors
```
mike: I'm going to flip the canary flag to 0 and initiate a canary rollback. Running:```
/rollout disable realtime-routing --canary --tag v2.7.0
```
pd-bot: Rollout disable command executed by mike at 1798887815 (job: rollback-1798887815).
lina: applying traffic diversion: updating traffic-split via console to route eu-west canary -> 0%, route stable -> 100%. Patch:```
PATCH /api/traffic-split
{ "region":"eu-west", "canary_pct": 0 }
```
sam: monitoring metrics: 5xx rate dropping in canary group. p99 latency returning to baseline. live graphs: https://grafana.internal/d/rvRt/canary-metrics
emma: also adjusting PD escalation to reduce duplicates: turned on dedupe window 300s for service realtime-routing-canary. That should stop multi-channel spam.
incident-bot: Suppression rule applied: dedupe_window=300s for PD-8231. Subsequent duplicate pages will be suppressed.
mike: rollback completed and stable traffic confirmed. tokenizer errors no longer observed in canary.
sam: confirming traces look normal; sample request trace: https://traces.internal/trace/7c3a -> shows upstream retry and success after divert.
support-engine: posting interim customer update: "We've detected a regression in a recent canary release affecting embeddings in EU-West. We have paused the canary and routed traffic back to stable. Engineers are investigating; we'll follow up with a postmortem." :wave:
emma: handing off to night oncall josh in 30m. I'll start a short postmortem draft and capture action items. Josh — can you take over monitoring and follow up with runtime/rlhf teams tomorrow?
josh: acked. I'll take the handoff at 1800 UTC, will keep monitoring and own the postmortem next shift.
emma: quick summary of action items: [1] root-cause: investigate tokenizer batch regression in v2.7.0 ci->deploy pipeline, [2] increase canary gating (add functional batch tests), [3] improve alert dedupe and PD routing to avoid duplicate channels, [4] customer comms follow-up.
mike: tagging for follow-up: @eng-runtime @eng-ml. I'll open RFC/issue with repro + logs.
emma: closing incident thread once we have stable metrics for 15m. Current status: degraded -> mitigated (traffic diverted + rollback). Will update postmortem link here. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident PD-8231 status: mitigated at 1798888389.
emma: incident closed. Postmortem draft: https://docs.internal/postmortems/PM-2026-03-realtime-routing-canary-batch-regress. Please add notes if you were involved.
